subject: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset - next steps

Hi Alex - thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the POC.

Recap (from our discussion):
- Goal: Validate Redwood's Retrieval-augmented generation flow to replace current in-house answers API for patient triage and care navigation.
- Top success criteria you called out: 1) >85% accuracy on clinical intent classification for triage prompts, 2) average latency <350ms at 8 RPS, 3) cost per 1k tokens under target by 20% vs current baseline.
- Data you'll provide: 250-500 representative prompts + 7 days of anonymized logs for coverage and distribution.

Proposed Evaluation Plan (high-level):
1) Prompt set collection - you provide prompts & example expected outputs where available (CSV or spreadsheet).
2) Redwood will create an eval dataset (derive references, categorize intents, and produce an initial scoring rubric).
3) Run baseline runs on open model variants we discussed; share quality + perf tradeoffs.
4) Joint review and pick a model/profile for a 2-week focused trial with live telemetry.

Timeline (target):
- You share prompt set + logs by Tue Apr 6
- Redwood returns initial eval dataset + plan by Fri Apr 9
- Trial window: Apr 12-Apr 26 (2 weeks)

Owners:
- AcmeHealth: Alex (data & prompts), legal for DPA if required
- Redwood: Marissa (POC lead), Marcus (CS lead - integration & runbook), Rishi (commercial/ops)

Action items for you: 
- Please upload the prompt set + anonymized logs to the shared Drive folder (suggested columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, user_intent, sample_response, timestamp).
- If possible, flag high-priority intents (top 10) and any compliance constraints for those prompts.

Attachments: I've attached a POC_prompt_template.xlsx (simple CSV tabs for prompts + expected outputs) to make collection easier.

Next meeting: propose Thu Apr 8 @ 10am PT for a quick alignment on the eval rubric (15-20m). If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks - looking forward to the dataset.

-
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset - next steps

Marissa - thanks for the thorough recap. That aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Prompt set size: we can get you ~300 prompts this week; is CSV fine?
2) Logs: we need to confirm with engineering on redaction but should be able to provide 7 days of anonymized request/response logs by Tue.
3) Success criteria: the >85% accuracy target is for classification/intent mapping only, not the freeform answer quality; we'll be evaluating quality separately (we can provide a small gold set).

I’m attaching an initial export (acme_prompts_v1.csv) with a sample of 50 prompts so you can start the rubric work. We’ll upload the full set + logs to the Drive once legal signs off on the anonymization process.

Two asks from us:
- Can Marcus own the integration checklist and quickstart?
- Will Redwood need any network/firewall details for the trial (we're on AWS, VPC)?

Happy to join Thu Apr 8 @ 10am PT.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Product | AcmeHealth
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com

Attachments: acme_prompts_v1.csv (CSV, 50 rows)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset - next steps

Thanks Alex - this is great and the sample is helpful. Confirming below and adding a couple operational notes.

1) CSV is perfect. Our template columns align with what you attached - we'll ingest that and produce the eval CSV and rubric.
2) Marcus will lead the integration checklist and runbook. Marcus - can you confirm you’re good to own the integration (VPC routing details, firewall, and test harness)?
3) On network: for the trial we’ll likely run from Redwood Private (VPC connector) or via dedicated-hosted endpoints depending on your preference. We’ll need a whitelist of egress IPs or an allowlist for our service endpoints - I’ll have Rishi follow up with exact IPs and any short-lived token approach if required.

Operational next steps: 
- Alex: upload full prompt set + anonymized logs to Drive by Tue Apr 6 (you mentioned legal signoff).
- Marcus: create the integration checklist doc in the shared Drive and confirm any firewall/VPC items by Mon Apr 5 EOD.
- Rishi: will prepare a short commercial note on capacity and expected credit for the trial; he’ll also share IP allowlist and test credentials.

We’ll also create a lightweight eval rubric (intent labels, pass/fail thresholds, and a quality bucket for freeform answers) and circulate before Thu’s sync.

I’ll send the calendar invite for Thu Apr 8 @ 10am PT. 

-
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset - next steps

Marissa / team - quick update: legal signed off on the anonymization approach this morning. I uploaded the full prompt set (300 rows) and 7 days of redacted logs to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-poc-prompts.

Marcus - I left comments on two prompts that are high-priority for triage (intent: urgent-care). Please let me know if you need any additional columns or context for the eval.

We’re good for Thu Apr 8 @ 10am PT. I’ll invite our engineer (Samir Patel) to the call for any network questions.

Thanks - looking forward to the rubric and baseline results.

Best,
Alex
